name: Victoria
summary: Northern and western Victoria remain the most watchful areas, with Melbourne metro and regional service corridors carrying the greatest public-footprint sensitivity.

name: New South Wales
summary: NSW is the clearest east-coast exposure, with northern and south-eastern regions capable of driving customer access and staff mobility disruption.

name: Queensland
summary: South-east Queensland combines fire-weather exposure, dense customer concentration and critical transport links into Brisbane and coastal growth areas.

name: Northern Territory
summary: Large parts of the Territory remain exposed through the dry season, with a lower-density but high-mobility risk profile.

name: Tasmania
summary: North-eastern Tasmania is the main spring watch area, with smaller local service networks more vulnerable to travel disruption.

name: South Australia
summary: South Australia carries a warmer and drier spring profile that can lift grassfire susceptibility, especially around the Adelaide interface.

name: Western Australia
summary: WA has a split outlook, with the south-west and urban-fringe interface areas most sensitive to fast-developing fire weather.

name: Australian Capital Territory
summary: The ACT is best treated as a secondary exposure tied to surrounding NSW fire conditions and smoke/road disruption.
